gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the two picks' length figures on one basis. The Cable Matters active extension is a 6.6 ft (2 m) cable; its '16.4 ft (5 m)' figure is how far the maker says it can extend an 8K run, which is not the cable's length (ChatGPT showed 'Up to 16.4 ft'). The UGREEN HD151 is a 0.5 m or 1 m cable that adds to the run's total length, and neither maker page claims the Ultra High Speed certification label that HDMI.org says certified cables carry.
standout_why: Pages compared: cablematters.com pc-1330-142 and pc-1330-139 (cited), bestways.com HD151 (cited), itechguides.com (cited), plus the uncited shinforce.com and bespokecable.com. The Cable Matters page states both numbers (Size 6.6 and 'extend an 8K cable run by 5 meters') but never says which one is the cable's length. ChatGPT read 16.4 ft as the length. itechguides and bespokecable say an extension adds to the total run and that you should check certification, but neither applies this to either pick. shinforce flags missing Ultra High Speed labels only on Highwings and Silkland, not on UGREEN or Cable Matters. No page sets the picks' stated length, reach, power and certification side by side, so rivals have parts of the finding but not the comparison.
decides: Confirms the split by distance but corrects the long-run pick. The Cable Matters active extension is 6.6 ft of cable and needs the female end at the source; its Micro-B power is optional, but the maker recommends it for longer runs and 8K. For a 10–20 ft extension, the shopper buys it as a 6.6 ft cable, not a 16.4 ft one. Neither maker page claims certification, and HDMI.org says certified cables must carry a label. For 4K120, a single certified cable at full length stays the safer buy, as ChatGPT's own caution said. UGREEN HD151 stays the short-gap pick at 0.5 or 1 m.
